title: RFID Food Reservation Terminal
summary: A Raspberry Pi terminal that retrieves daily reservation data, checks RFID cards and guides the operator through meal-distribution states.
problem: Connect a daily reservation list to the physical collection point and distinguish eligible, unreserved and repeated collection attempts.
approach: Received the daily reservation list automatically from a server.
Used RFID cards to identify the reservation at the terminal.
Built a Tkinter interface for reservation and meal-distribution states.
outcome: An embedded meal-reservation workflow with original hardware imagery, four interface states and a running-system demonstration.
role: Python application development and embedded integration

sections.title: From the daily list to the service point
body: The terminal retrieves reservation data from a web server at a scheduled time and starts the distribution workflow during configured periods. RFID cards let users check their reservation at the Raspberry Pi device.

sections.title: An interface for the situations that matter
body: The Tkinter application distinguishes a valid reservation, no reservation, an already delivered meal and the end of distribution. These states give the operator immediate context at the collection point.

sections.title: Connecting software and the reader
body: Python implements the application, with serial communication for the RF01D reader and GPIO for embedded integration. The hardware comprises a Raspberry Pi, the card reader and a custom single-layer PCB.

sections.title: Original implementation views
body: The project media covers the main window, the circuit and RFID card, the completion state and a recording of the system running.

result: An embedded meal-reservation workflow with original hardware imagery, four interface states and a running-system demonstration.
decisionNotes: The terminal retrieves a daily reservation list from a server at a scheduled time and checks RF01D card identifiers against reservation and prior-collection states. Tkinter distinguishes valid, unreserved, already-delivered and completed-distribution states on the Raspberry Pi.
validationNotes: Original interface and circuit photographs accompany a terminal demonstration and a bench recording with several card and status changes. Personal details are masked in the bench recording. These demonstrate the workflow; no throughput, deployment count or long-duration service-reliability measurement is supplied.
